previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and a tracheostomy was admitted after accidentally dislodging his GJ tube at his nursing home. He was unable to take his morning medications and was found to have leukocytosis and tachycardia. He received IV fluids and a dose of metoprolol, which resolved his tachycardia. A temporary Foley catheter was placed to maintain the gastrostomy tract, and the GJ tube was successfully replaced the following day under fluoroscopic guidance. His leukocytosis improved without antibiotics, and urine culture showed mixed flora consistent with colonization rather than infection. He remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Chronic issues including HIV, seizures, COPD, and abdominal pain were managed with his home medications. The decision was made to remove his chronic indwelling Foley catheter as an outpatient due to infection risk. He was discharged back to extended care after a two-day stay.

microbiology.comments: HIV-1 RNA detected, less than 20 copies/mL.  Performed using the ___ HIV-1 Test v2.0.  Detection Range: 20-10,000,000 copies/mL.  This test is approved for monitoring HIV-1 viral load in known HIV-positive patients. It is not approved for diagnosis of acute HIV infection.  In symptomatic acute HIV infection (acute retroviral syndrome), the viral load is usually very high (>>1000 copies/mL). If acute HIV infection is clinically suspected and there is a detectable but low viral load, please contact the laboratory for interpretation.  It is recommended that any NEW positive HIV-1 viral load result, in the absence of positive serology, be confirmed by submitting a new sample FOR HIV-1 PCR, in addition to serological testing.
